questions.q: What are the biotic and abiotic parts of an ecosystem?
questions.a: Biotic: all living organisms. Abiotic: non-living factors like air, water, soil, temperature and light.

questions.q: How does energy flow in an ecosystem?
questions.a: One way: sunlight -> producers -> herbivores -> carnivores, with about 10% passing to each level.

questions.q: Why is the number of trophic levels limited?
questions.a: Energy shrinks tenfold at each transfer, leaving too little to sustain more levels.

questions.q: Why is the ozone layer called a protective shield?
questions.a: It absorbs the sun's harmful ultraviolet rays that would damage living cells.
Chlorofluorocarbons used in refrigerators and sprays.

questions.q: What steps protect the ozone layer?
questions.a: Phasing out CFCs under global agreements and using safer alternatives.

concepts.title: Managing Our Garbage - Biodegradable and Non-biodegradable Waste

questions.q: Distinguish biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste with examples.
questions.a: Biodegradable waste rots naturally (vegetable peels, paper); non-biodegradable waste does not (plastics, glass).

questions.q: Why is segregation of waste at source important?
questions.a: Separating wet and dry waste lets organic waste be composted and recyclables recovered, cutting landfill load.
Using redworms to convert biodegradable waste into rich compost.
